hardware.execution: Windows Go API, load generator and native Centrifugo share this machine; PostgreSQL 18.6 in Docker Linux temporary memory storage

adopted.page_cache: Ristretto v2.4.2, estimated-cost budget 64 MiB, TTL 5 minutes, exact content-key check and cloned results; current database membership and stream position checked before every read
adopted.coalescing: existing golang.org/x/sync v0.24.0 singleflight, content loads only; canceled leader may fail shared waiters, failures not cached
adopted.outbox: sixth migration, generated control partition 0 and scope-stable data partitions 1..4; transactional notification plus existing 20ms polling fallback
adopted.admission: per-counter 2 active, 12 active/waiting; global 12 active for pool 16, 256 active/waiting, 2-second shared wait deadline; single instance only

notes: Same fixed-arrival four fanout scenarios, 3-second warmup and 12-second measured launch window. History 100/s with 32 workers; ordinary writes 25/s with 8 workers; hot input uses 32 workers per stream. No automatic retries.

The baseline binary was frozen before implementation: five migrations, one consumer partition, no page cache. Candidates embed the sixth migration and five consumer partitions. Each run starts a fresh isolated synthetic fixture.
One baseline, one cache/partition/notification candidate and two final repetitions. This is a bundled comparison, not a factorial attribution of gains to cache, partitions or notifications.
Stream UUIDs differ between runs, so collisions across four data partitions are not held fixed. Client/server/SDK callback CPU and process scheduling remain shared.

Cache statistics cover content only. Every hit still incurs the database identity and current membership/stream-position lookups. Measured hit rate reflects a warmed repetitive-prefix workload, not production behavior.

HTTP latency includes every started attempt. Send-to-receive uses the same monotonic clock and only actually committed/delivered events. Refused and unsent demand remain separate and are never counted as delivered.

Each phase checks request ID to database author/body/root/quote/continuous position and canonical payload plus event identity at every receiver. All expected committed copies matched, with no missing/invalid/duplicate/out-of-order events in these tests.
The new fanout and short API harnesses validate write-capacity problem code and Retry-After: 1. Frozen baseline only classified status. No claim that all offered input succeeded.

The short final benchmark explicitly counts capacity refusals, and success throughput excludes refusals. Its 32-concurrent one-stream burst intentionally has no backoff: high refusal count is retained as a regression/tradeoff, not relabeled speed.

Short baseline fields succeeded and capacity_rejected were absent; normalized as requests and zero because all original errors were zero. Synthetic UUID literals in EXPLAIN are redacted, raw file hashes are retained.

Upgrade and downgrade require stopped writers, drained outbox and a synchronized switch of all consumers. Nonempty migration fails before routing changes; no online rerouting of backlog or mixed one/five-partition consumers.

P2 backend remains complete. Current product mode is threaded; instant-style posts and fixed product channels remain P3. P6 production capacity, real disk/network/slow-client/refresh/soak and encryption deployment remain unaccepted.

verification.full_regression: passed; postgres 87.702s; includes real 65-second outage, expiry, two-node recovery/revocation and partition isolation; later changes restricted to performance reporting, equivalent SQL constant extraction and default cache tests
verification.cleanup: owned Compose containers and networks absent, native Centrifugo process count zero

trials.variant: cache, five logical outbox partitions and notification; shared scope queue unchanged
